title: Reliable, antigen-specific immune tolerance

concept.text: The innovation would make the immune system durably accept a selected donor graft or antigen while retaining its ability to respond to infections and other threats. In transplantation, the intended outcome is sustained graft function without rejection or maintenance immunosuppression, achieved with acceptable treatment risks. Reduced drug requirements are meaningful progress, but do not by themselves demonstrate this complete capability.

The supplied clinical example pursues this goal through hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation after solid-organ transplantation, using a graft depleted of naive T cells. This belongs to a broader approach involving donor-derived blood-forming cells and chimerism: the presence of donor-derived hematopoietic cells within the recipient. The engineering challenge includes cell preparation, conditioning, immune reprogramming and monitoring. Evidence from this approach concerns donor-associated transplant tolerance; it does not establish a general method for inducing tolerance to any chosen antigen.

significance.text: Reliable selective tolerance could substantially change transplantation by removing the need for broad, ongoing immunosuppression. The supplied report describes the association of chronic immunosuppression with infection, cardiovascular disease and cancer. If a tolerance-inducing intervention safely replaced maintenance treatment, it could reduce this treatment burden while preserving the graft. The net benefit would depend on whether the intervention and any conditioning introduce fewer or more manageable risks than the treatment they replace.

The essential advance would be selective acceptance, rather than simply weaker immune activity. A functioning graft accompanied by low donor-reactive responses and retained responses to unrelated challenges would be more informative than graft survival alone. The reported preservation of cytomegalovirus (CMV) responses in two patients is encouraging within that narrow scope, but cannot establish protection against infections generally or normal vaccine responses.

Conditional synthesis: a broadly usable tolerance platform could also make other replacement-tissue technologies more useful by addressing immune acceptance after implantation. Extension to autoimmune disease could be consequential, but accepting a donor graft and selectively suppressing a disease-causing response to self-antigens are distinct clinical problems. Each autoimmune application would require its own evidence of target specificity, disease control and preserved protective immunity.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is a reproducible way to establish durable, selective tolerance across diverse recipients and transplant settings without dangerous conditioning or generalized immune impairment. The supplied article identifies conditioning requirements and restriction of many existing approaches to elective living-donor procedures as practical limitations. These constraints leave unresolved how to make treatment safe, broadly applicable and compatible with transplant circumstances beyond carefully selected protocols.

A central scientific and clinical barrier is determining when graft acceptance reflects a sufficiently selective and durable immune change to permit safe withdrawal of immunosuppression. Continued drug treatment complicates interpretation: rejection-free follow-up on monotherapy does not show that the same graft would remain protected without that treatment. The 2026 report explicitly calls for larger cohorts and prospective trials before withdrawal can be justified following its intervention.

Further work must connect immune measurements to clinical outcomes. Low donor-reactive responses need to be interpreted alongside responses to unrelated antigens, infection outcomes and the effects of ongoing medication. The supplied evidence does not establish a validated immune-test threshold that predicts safe withdrawal. Nor does it resolve how reliably this approach could tolerate an arbitrary chosen antigen or treat autoimmune disease.

current_state.text: The supplied article's literature summary reports that some kidney-transplant protocols using donor hematopoietic-cell treatment have enabled withdrawal of immunosuppression. It also describes continuing limitations involving conditioning and applicability, including reliance by many approaches on elective living-donor procedures. The underlying kidney studies were not supplied for direct inspection in the review, so this is a secondary account of prior progress rather than an independently assessed description of their outcomes or eligibility boundaries.

On 21 September 2026, Antonio Pérez-Martínez and colleagues published a two-patient case report of naive T cell-depleted hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation following solid-organ transplantation. The report described no signs of rejection after 6 and 5.2 years of follow-up, with recipients remaining on sirolimus or tacrolimus monotherapy. These observations demonstrate prolonged graft acceptance with minimized immunosuppression in two cases. They do not demonstrate complete drug withdrawal, establish that the intervention caused the outcomes, or show reliability across a diverse patient population.

The article contains an unresolved inconsistency in its immune-response reporting. Its abstract describes hyporesponsiveness to both donor and third-party cells, whereas the detailed results and the reviewed supplementary table show low donor responses with substantially greater third-party responses. For Patient 1, the detailed results report donor-response measurements of 0.79% and 0.94%, compared with third-party measurements of 7.27% and 10.5%. Supplementary Table 5's CD3+CD8+ CFSE-low row reports donor versus third-party values of 0.79% versus 7.27% for Patient 1 and 0.29% versus 44.7% for Patient 2. These measurements support a difference between donor and third-party responses within the reported assays, but do not establish normal immune competence relative to healthy controls or resolve the conflicting abstract wording.

CMV responses were retained in the reported experiments. This provides limited evidence that immune reactivity was not uniformly absent, but it does not establish broad infection protection, vaccine competence or drug-free tolerance. The two heterogeneous cases remain preliminary clinical evidence, and the authors state that their ultimate goal of a regimen without immunosuppression was not fully achieved.

The supplied review had complete main-article text in HTML and an 11-page PDF, but these are copies of the same study rather than independent confirmation. Figure images were not inspected. Supplementary extraction was partial: the relevant Table 5 headers and measurements were available, while Table 7's data were absent from the supplied extraction. These limits constrain interpretation of the full experimental record without negating the available clinical observations or Table 5 measurements.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: randomized studies across different transplant settings and diverse recipients would show sustained graft function without rejection or maintenance immunosuppression over prespecified long-term follow-up. Protocols would define withdrawal procedures, rejection surveillance, rescue treatment and acceptable treatment and conditioning risks in advance. These are proposed assessment criteria, not established consensus standards; the supplied evidence does not justify a particular universal follow-up duration or numerical success threshold.
completion_criteria.label: Sustained graft function without rejection or maintenance immunosuppression

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration of selectivity: donor-specific immune testing would be paired with unrelated-antigen responses, clinically observed infection outcomes and vaccine-response measurements. Together, these would test whether graft acceptance coexists with useful protective immunity. A single retained antiviral response or an isolated donor-reactivity assay would provide only part of that evidence.
completion_criteria.label: Donor-specific graft acceptance coexists with useful protective immunity

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: independent teams and centers would reproduce the outcomes with sufficiently specified cell-processing, conditioning, treatment and monitoring procedures. Studies would report which recipient groups, donor relationships and organ types were included, where treatment failed, and whether its risks and logistics permit routine use. Finite trials would establish demonstrated breadth within those conditions, rather than literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Independent centers reproduce outcomes and report practical treatment boundaries

completion_criteria.text: Proposed extension beyond transplantation: separate disease-specific trials would establish whether selected autoimmune responses can be controlled durably while protective immunity is retained. Success in donor-associated graft acceptance would not alone complete the broader chosen-antigen ambition.
completion_criteria.label: Disease-specific trials demonstrate durable autoimmune control with protective immunity

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BME-01, Manufacturing transplantable human organs on demand, addresses organ supply, while BME-06, Long-term banking of transplantable human organs, addresses preservation and availability. BME-08 addresses immune acceptance after transplantation. These capabilities could complement one another, but making or storing an organ does not establish tolerance, and tolerance does not solve organ production or preservation.

Roster-based synthesis: BME-12, Reliable, scalable animal-to-human organ transplantation, shares the problem of immune acceptance but concerns transplantation across species and has a broader completion burden. The supplied human transplant evidence does not establish tolerance to animal-derived organs or complete the animal-to-human transplantation concept.

Roster-based synthesis: BME-05, Programmable living medicines that sense and respond inside the body, overlaps with BME-08 when engineered cells are used to regulate immunity. Its defining capability is sensing and responding within the body; BME-08's defining outcome is durable, selective tolerance. BME-02, Programmable delivery of genetic therapies to most tissues, could offer enabling delivery methods, but successful delivery alone would not establish immune tolerance.

Roster-based synthesis: BME-16, Long-lived tissue-integrated interfaces for implants, and BME-13, Durable autonomous artificial-organ replacement, both concern sustained compatibility between a therapeutic device and the body. Antigen-specific graft tolerance would not by itself solve the full biological, material and functional requirements of implanted interfaces or artificial organs. BME-17, Minimally invasive assembly of functional tissue inside the body, could intersect with tolerance when introduced tissue presents immune targets, while retaining its distinct challenge of assembling functional tissue.

change_log.reason: The detailed results and supplementary Table 5 report substantially greater third-party than donor responses; the inconsistency remains unresolved.

change_log.change: Distinguished retained CMV responses from general infection protection and vaccine competence.
change_log.reason: A narrow antiviral assay cannot establish comprehensive protective immunity.

change_log.change: Focused the missing breakthrough on documented conditioning, applicability, withdrawal and immune-selectivity challenges.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence does not establish immune memory or loss of established tolerance as demonstrated obstacles in these cases.

change_log.change: Expanded proposed completion criteria to include graft function, rejection, conditioning risk, immune selectivity, reproducibility and practical eligibility boundaries.
change_log.reason: These make the proposed demonstration assessable without presenting it as a published standard or claiming finite trials can establish universality.

unresolved_issues: The abstract's characterization of third-party hyporesponsiveness conflicts with the detailed results and supplementary Table 5. The supplied material contains no author clarification resolving it.
The available immune-response measurements do not establish normal-control equivalence, broad infection protection or vaccine competence.
Whether recipients treated with this intervention can safely discontinue maintenance immunosuppression remains unestablished.
The underlying kidney-protocol studies were not supplied for direct review, leaving their detailed outcomes, eligibility conditions and risks unassessed here.
Figure images were not inspected, and supplementary Table 7 data were absent from the supplied extraction; their implications cannot be resolved from the provided review.
Reliability across diverse recipients, transplant settings, arbitrary chosen antigens and autoimmune diseases remains unestablished.
Immune memory and loss of established tolerance were not retained as evidence-established barriers because the supplied source does not substantiate those original assertions.
The supplied freshness record is empty, so the review does not establish whether the September 2026 report represents the latest available evidence.

brief.title: Lasting immune acceptance without losing protection
possible: People receiving a donor organ could keep it working without lifelong anti-rejection drugs. Their immune system would accept the transplant while still responding to infections and vaccines.

The broader goal is to stop an immune attack on a chosen target without weakening other defenses. This could also help people with autoimmune diseases, in which the immune system attacks the body’s own tissues.
why: Transplant recipients could avoid the burden of ongoing immune suppression and its associated risks, including infection, cardiovascular disease and cancer.
Reliable immune acceptance could also make implanted replacement tissues more useful by addressing rejection.

sources.showed: A small case report described lasting organ acceptance after patients received blood-forming stem cells from their organ donor. Patients continued taking low-dose anti-rejection medicine.
sources.quote: Several years later, both patients remain stable, have no signs of organ rejection, and only need very low doses of anti-rejection medicines.
sources.cited_for: Donor blood-forming cells may help reduce the need for anti-rejection drugs.
sources.not_established: The report did not demonstrate acceptance without drugs or establish that the treatment caused the outcomes.

sources.who: Stephan Busque and colleagues at Stanford University
sources.showed: Selected kidney recipients with closely matched living donors stopped anti-rejection drugs after receiving donor blood-forming cells. Less closely matched recipients experienced rejection when treatment stopped.
sources.quote: No evidence of rejection was observed in all surveillance graft biopsies obtained from mixed chimeric patients withdrawn from IS drugs, and none developed graft-versus-host disease.
sources.cited_for: Drug-free kidney acceptance is possible when donor and recipient blood-forming cells coexist, a state called mixed chimerism.
sources.not_established: Success in selected matched recipients does not establish reliable acceptance across donor matches or organ types.

sources.showed: Three kidney recipients with closely matched sibling donors stopped anti-rejection drugs and retained vaccine responses. Donated immune cells did not attack their bodies, a complication called graft-versus-host disease.
sources.quote: No rejection or graft-versus-host disease occurred.
sources.cited_for: A separate team reproduced drug-free kidney acceptance with evidence of retained vaccine responses.
sources.not_established: The small sibling-donor trial does not establish broad applicability or protection against infections generally.

sources.showed: A kidney recipient later rejected the organ despite a low donor response in a mixed lymphocyte reaction (MLR), a laboratory immune test.
sources.quote: At that time, the MLR still showed a low response to the donor.
sources.cited_for: Weak laboratory responses to donor cells do not guarantee lasting acceptance after drug withdrawal.
sources.not_established: The case does not establish a reliable test for deciding when anti-rejection drugs can safely stop.

sources.who: Ciarán P Kelly and colleagues, on behalf of the TAK-101 Study Group
sources.showed: In a small randomized trial, TAK-101, tiny particles carrying gluten protein, reduced gluten-triggered immune activity in celiac disease (CeD), an immune disorder triggered by gluten.
sources.quote: TAK-101 was well tolerated and prevented gluten-induced immune activation in CeD.
sources.cited_for: Treatment can reduce an immune response to a specific target beyond transplantation.
sources.not_established: The trial did not establish lasting disease control, clear protection from intestinal damage or broadly preserved protective immunity.

shown: Stanford researchers achieved complete anti-rejection drug withdrawal in 24 selected kidney recipients with closely matched donors. They combined kidney transplantation with donor blood-forming cells.

A small Zurich trial reproduced drug-free kidney acceptance and found retained vaccine responses. Pérez-Martínez and colleagues reported prolonged acceptance after other organ transplants, but their patients continued anti-rejection medicine.
missing: Treatment has yet to work reliably across diverse recipients and transplant settings with acceptable risks from preparatory treatment.
No validated immune-test threshold predicts when anti-rejection drugs can safely stop.
Lasting control of selected autoimmune responses, together with preserved protective immunity, remains to be demonstrated.

milestones.label: Transplants keep working without anti-rejection drugs
milestones.explanation: Randomized studies across diverse recipients and transplant settings would have to show lasting organ function without rejection or ongoing drugs, at acceptable treatment risk. This would establish reliable drug-free acceptance.

milestones.label: Transplant acceptance preserves useful immune defenses
milestones.explanation: Donor-response tests, unrelated immune responses, infection outcomes and vaccine responses would have to show preserved protection alongside acceptance. This would distinguish selective acceptance from broad immune weakening.

milestones.label: Independent centers reproduce results and define treatment limits
milestones.explanation: Independent centers would have to reproduce outcomes with clearly described procedures and report eligible patients, failures, risks and logistics. This would establish where routine treatment is practical.

milestones.label: Autoimmune disease stays controlled while immune protection remains
milestones.explanation: Separate disease-specific trials would have to show lasting control of selected autoimmune responses while preserving protective immunity. This would establish whether selective acceptance extends beyond donor organs.

uncertain: It remains unclear how much donor and recipient blood-forming cells must coexist, and for how long, to sustain acceptance.
The Pérez-Martínez report conflicts internally about responses to unrelated cells, leaving the selectivity of its immune effects uncertain.
The follow-up duration and success rate needed to judge reliable tolerance across settings remain open.

page.title: Reliable donor-specific transplantation tolerance
page.definition: A finite treatment makes most organ recipients who receive it, including those mismatched with their donor for human leukocyte antigens (HLA, the proteins used in tissue matching), accept the graft without maintenance immunosuppression while keeping immune responses to other antigens. Reliability is shown by a multicentre randomized trial, not by selected patients.

goal.need: The United States performed 48,149 organ transplants in 2024, including 27,759 kidney and 11,458 liver transplants, according to preliminary OPTN data. NIAID identifies infection, malignancy and atherosclerosis as risks of systemic immunosuppression and makes donor-specific tolerance a goal for avoiding that treatment burden.

figures.caption: United States transplant procedures in 2024: preliminary OPTN counts.
figures.note: Procedure counts describe transplantation volume, not eligibility for tolerance protocols.

statements.body: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases
statements.quote: Tolerance induction strategies aim to selectively block or prevent deleterious immune responses, while leaving protective immunity intact.
achieve the complete and planned withdrawal of all immunosuppression while maintaining the healthy function of the graft organ.
statements.context: The stated primary goal of the network's interventional transplantation studies.

completion.title: A multicentre randomized trial shows drug-free graft acceptance in most HLA-mismatched recipients.
completion.criterion: A randomized, controlled, multicentre trial of a tolerance-induction treatment in HLA-mismatched organ recipients meets a prespecified primary endpoint of freedom from all immunosuppression without biopsy-proven acute rejection at least 24 months after transplantation and at least 12 months after complete drug withdrawal. At least 50 recipients are treated and at least half of all those treated reach the endpoint. Drug-free recipients show immune responses to non-donor antigens, for example to vaccination. The result is reported in a peer-reviewed paper or a regulator's review.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas. The endpoint is the primary outcome of the FREEDOM-1 phase 3 protocol (NCT03995901), the 12 drug-free months the operational-tolerance convention, and immunocompetence the Immune Tolerance Network objective; the HLA-mismatched scope, 50 treated and one half are the Atlas's.
completion.threshold_quote: Proportion of FCR001 recipients who are free from immunosuppression (IS), without biopsy proven acute rejection (BPAR) at 24 months post-transplant
completion.basis: No regulator, society or programme document located states a trial size or success fraction for tolerance induction. The Atlas sets them: half of those treated is the least that "most recipients" can mean, and with 50 treated the 95% confidence interval on a proportion near one half is about 14 percentage points either side. HLA-mismatched recipients are required because results in HLA-matched siblings do not carry over to most transplants. Marketing authorization is a separate, later event.

milestones.title: A treated animal accepts donor tissue and rejects third-party tissue without maintenance immunosuppression.
milestones.criterion: The animal retains its organ graft, accepts a second donor graft and rejects an unrelated donor's graft after maintenance drugs stop. Kidney: skin-graft testing supported tolerance in 5 of 6 long-surviving rhesus recipients in 1997. Heart/kidney: 1 of 5 challenged cynomolgus recipients accepted donor skin indefinitely; all 5 rejected third-party skin in the 2025 report. Lung: 1 recipient in a 6-monkey study accepted donor skin for over 134 days and rejected third-party skin in 20 days in 2015.
milestones.set_by: Experimental transplantation convention, stated by Ezekian and colleagues in Contemporary Strategies and Barriers to Transplantation Tolerance.
milestones.threshold_quote: a second graft from the same donor should be accepted, whereas a graft from a third-party donor should be rejected.

milestones.title: An organ recipient has no rejection or graft-versus-host disease at 6 and 12 months.
milestones.criterion: Following donor hematopoietic-cell transplantation, assess absence of organ rejection and graft-versus-host disease at 6 and 12 months. The latter is donor immune cells attacking recipient tissues. Zurich reported no such events in 3 HLA-identical kidney recipients. A report published on 21 September 2026 described 2 recipients, one multivisceral including intestine and kidney and one kidney-only, without rejection or graft-versus-host disease after 6 and 5.2 years, respectively; both continued immunosuppressive monotherapy.
milestones.set_by: University Hospital Zurich, NCT00365846 secondary endpoints; written for HLA-identical sibling kidney and hematopoietic-cell transplantation.
milestones.threshold_quote: absence of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after 6 and 12 months, absence of renal allograft rejection at 6 and 12 months

milestones.title: An organ recipient maintains graft function for at least 1 year without immunosuppressive drugs.
milestones.criterion: Maintain stable graft function without clinical rejection or overt immunodeficiency for at least 1 year after complete drug withdrawal. Kidney: Stanford withdrew drugs in 24 of 29 fully HLA-matched recipients; 23 of 24 remained rejection-free during follow-up of up to 10 years, although 4 resumed drugs. Liver: LIFT found biopsy-defined tolerance in 13 of 80 withdrawal participants at 12 months. Intestine: 1 recipient remained drug-free for 5 years with donor hyporesponsiveness and antiviral responses; withdrawal was spontaneous, not a planned induction.
milestones.set_by: Clinical operational-tolerance convention summarized by Massart and colleagues; minimum duration documented for kidney transplantation. Liver evidence additionally uses LIFT biopsy criteria.
milestones.threshold_quote: All authors agreed upon a strict minimal period of 1 year without immunosuppression before evoking tolerance.

milestones.title: An organ recipient remains off all immunosuppressive drugs for more than 2 years in a randomized trial.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate sustained drug withdrawal in a randomized clinical trial. In NCT03363945, adults receiving kidneys from two-haplotype HLA-matched living siblings received MDR-101 donor cells or standard care. Withdrawal was conditional on donor blood-cell chimerism of at least 5%. Of 20 treated recipients and 10 controls, 19 treated recipients stopped all drugs around 1 year after transplantation and 15 remained off for more than 2 years; 4 restarted. This endpoint establishes functional tolerance without directly testing unrelated immunity.
milestones.set_by: Medeor Therapeutics, NCT03363945 primary endpoint, reported by Kaufman and colleagues in 2025; written for HLA-matched living-sibling kidney transplantation.
milestones.threshold_quote: Fifteen (75%) reached the primary study endpoint of IS-free for >2 years.

milestones.title: A drug-free organ recipient with stable graft function retains immune responses to non-donor antigens.
milestones.criterion: After a tolerance-inducing intervention and complete withdrawal of immunosuppressive drugs, clinical assessment, laboratory tests and histology show normal or stable graft function, and the recipient shows immunocompetence to non-donor antigens, for example a protective response to vaccination or reactivity to third-party cells in vitro. ITN specifies no minimum follow-up, success fraction or immune-assay cutoff.
milestones.set_by: Immune Tolerance Network, Strategic Plan: Transplantation, Clinical Objectives.
milestones.threshold_quote: normal and/or stable allograft function, in the absence of generalized immunosuppression with concurrent immunocompetence to non-donor antigens.

milestones.title: Most HLA-mismatched recipients in a prospective study are drug-free without rejection at 24 months.
milestones.criterion: In a prospective study of a tolerance-induction treatment given to at least 10 HLA-mismatched organ recipients, more than half of all those treated are free from immunosuppression without biopsy-proven acute rejection 24 months after transplantation. Free from immunosuppression means taking no immunosuppressive drug since withdrawal. A single-centre or uncontrolled study suffices.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas. The endpoint is the primary outcome of the FREEDOM-1 phase 3 protocol (NCT03995901); the HLA-mismatched scope, the minimum of 10 treated and the majority are the Atlas's.
milestones.threshold_quote: Proportion of FCR001 recipients who are free from immunosuppression (IS), without biopsy proven acute rejection (BPAR) at 24 months post-transplant

not_found: No common completion test spanning donor-graft tolerance and tolerance to arbitrary autoimmune targets was located.
The 2025 MDR-101 publisher full text and ClinicalTrials.gov outcome fields were not readable; the authors' institutional abstract was accessible.
No prospective human heart or lung tolerance-induction result meeting the full ITN objective was located.
No FDA guidance, Immune Tolerance Network document or society consensus was located that states a minimum trial size or success fraction for tolerance induction.

results.finding: Among 108 liver transplant recipients with paired biopsies, 43.5% achieved operational tolerance.
results.detail: All 287 cohort participants had complete immunosuppression withdrawal for at least 12 months. The abstract does not define operational tolerance or report whether those patients had clinical rejection or overt immunodeficiency.
results.quote: Paired liver biopsies before and after ISW were available in 108 patients (37.6%) and among them 43.5% achieved operational tolerance.

results.finding: One intestinal transplant recipient maintained graft acceptance and immune competence 5 years after stopping immunosuppression.
results.detail: Withdrawal was self-directed. Graft assessments at 2 and 3 years showed no rejection; antiviral responses and donor-specific hyporesponsiveness were demonstrated. Donor-specific antibodies persisted.
results.quote: In contrast, our case demonstrated evidence of clinical organ acceptance (no rejection), immunocompetence to third party antigen, and donor-specific hyporesponsiveness even five years after stopping all immunosuppression.

results.finding: Two kidney recipients had no rejection or GvHD through at least 5.2 years after combined organ and hematopoietic-cell transplantation.
results.detail: Patient #1 received a kidney with a multivisceral graft and remained event-free for 6 years; Patient #2 received a kidney alone. Both continued immunosuppressive monotherapy.
results.quote: The patient has had no acute rejection, GvHD, kidney failure, viral reactivations, or bacterial infections after a follow‑up period of more than 5 years (5.2 years).

results.finding: One liver-containing multivisceral recipient had no rejection or GvHD through 6 years.
results.detail: Patient #1 received donor hematopoietic cells after multivisceral and kidney transplantation and continued sirolimus monotherapy.
results.quote: The patient did not experience acute rejection, graft-versus-host disease (GvHD), or viral reactivation, maintaining 100% Lansky performance status after a follow-up period of 6 years.

results.finding: One intestine-containing multivisceral recipient had no rejection or GvHD through 6 years.
results.detail: Patient #1 received donor hematopoietic cells after multivisceral and kidney transplantation and continued sirolimus monotherapy.
results.quote: The patient did not experience acute rejection, graft-versus-host disease (GvHD), or viral reactivation, maintaining 100% Lansky performance status after a follow-up period of 6 years.

results.finding: Among 22 haplotype-matched kidney recipients, 10 with persistent chimerism had no clinical rejection through the first year; no GVHD was reported.
results.detail: Recipients received donor hematopoietic cells. The 10 persistent chimeras remained on immunosuppression through 6 and 12 months; six had surveillance biopsies without rejection at 360–487 days.
results.quote: Partial or complete withdrawal of IS drugs was not associated with rejection or GVHD in persistent chimeric recipients, and persistence is likely to provide continued prevention of rejection.

results.finding: Among 3 combined kidney and hematopoietic-cell recipients, none developed rejection or graft-versus-host disease through 12 months.
results.detail: HLA-identical sibling recipients were followed beyond both assessment points; nine allograft biopsies showed no rejection, and no acute or chronic graft-versus-host disease occurred.
results.quote: No rejection or graft-versus-host disease occurred.

results.finding: One kidney/hematopoietic stem-cell recipient developed acute T cell-mediated rejection 356 days after transplantation.
results.detail: No graft-versus-host disease was reported during follow-up, but rejection near the 12-month assessment prevents meeting the criterion.
results.quote: At 127 days after discontinuation of immunosuppressant (356 days after KT), the serum creatinine level increased abruptly from 0.85 to 2.94 mg/dL, and a kidney biopsy showed acute T cell-mediated rejection, type IIA.

results.finding: Among 37 kidney/FCR001 recipients, 1 patient developed fatal graft-versus-host disease.
results.detail: The study reports rejection and graft-versus-host disease outcomes after donor hematopoietic-cell transplantation, but does not establish absence of both at the specified 6- and 12-month assessments.
results.quote:
1  
patient developed graft-versus-host disease, returned to IS, 
and eventually expired

results.finding: One lung/BMT recipient experienced minimal acute cellular rejection approximately 11 months after BMT.
results.detail: A1 rejection occurred 15 months after lung transplantation, with BMT performed 4 months after transplantation. Transient skin GvHD also occurred earlier after donor leukocyte infusion. Event-free outcomes at both specified checkpoints are not established.
results.quote: only a single biopsy (15 months after BOLT while still on tacrolimus) showed A1 (“minimal” acute cellular rejection)

results.finding: Among 20 MDR-101-treated kidney recipients, none developed graft-versus-host disease.
results.detail: Rejection occurred in two recipients who restarted immunosuppression; another had borderline biopsy changes. Absence of both rejection and graft-versus-host disease at 6 and 12 months is not reported.
results.quote: Twenty recipients received the MDR-101 infusion, and none developed graft versus host disease.

results.finding: One intestinal transplant recipient maintained graft acceptance and immunocompetence for 5 years after stopping all immunosuppression.
results.detail: Withdrawal was spontaneous, against medical advice, rather than following a tolerance-inducing intervention. Follow-up included normal graft function, rejection-free histology, donor-specific hyporesponsiveness and preserved antiviral responses.
results.quote: In contrast, our case demonstrated evidence of clinical organ acceptance (no rejection), immunocompetence to third party antigen, and donor-specific hyporesponsiveness even five years after stopping all immunosuppression.

results.finding: Among 20 MDR-101 kidney recipients, none developed graft-versus-host disease.
results.detail: Rejection occurred in recipients who resumed immunosuppression. The text does not report combined absence of rejection and graft-versus-host disease at both 6 and 12 months.
results.quote: Twenty recipients received the MDR-101 infusion, and none developed graft versus host disease.

results.finding: Two kidney-containing graft recipients remained rejection-free for more than 5 years under maintenance monotherapy.
results.detail: Patient #1 received a multivisceral graft including a kidney; Patient #2 received a kidney alone. Neither stopped all immunosuppression: sirolimus and tacrolimus, respectively, continued.
results.quote: Both patients were maintained in minimal immunosuppression with no signs of rejection more than 5 years after the SOT/HSCT.

results.finding: One liver-containing multivisceral graft recipient remained without acute rejection through 6 years of follow-up.
results.detail: Patient #1 continued sirolimus maintenance. The result concerns the combined multivisceral transplant; complete drug withdrawal was not achieved.
results.quote: The patient did not experience acute rejection, graft-versus-host disease (GvHD), or viral reactivation, maintaining 100% Lansky performance status after a follow-up period of 6 years.

results.finding: One intestine-containing multivisceral graft recipient remained without acute rejection through 6 years of follow-up.
results.detail: Patient #1 continued sirolimus maintenance. Complete withdrawal of immunosuppressive drugs was not achieved.
results.quote: The patient did not experience acute rejection, graft-versus-host disease (GvHD), or viral reactivation, maintaining 100% Lansky performance status after a follow-up period of 6 years.

results.finding: Both kidney-containing graft recipients (2/2) retained CMV reactivity after the intervention while maintaining stable graft function.
results.detail: Immune testing occurred at 41 and 31 months. Both remained on maintenance immunosuppression, so neither met the drug-free requirement. The report does not establish stable graft histology for both.
results.quote: Recipient cells resulted hyporesponsive to donor and third-party cells, yet retained reactivity to CMV infection.

results.finding: One liver-containing multivisceral graft recipient retained CMV reactivity at 41 months after transplantation.
results.detail: Patient #1 had stable, rejection-free multivisceral graft function and demonstrated antiviral responses, but remained on sirolimus. The drug-free requirement was not met; liver-specific histological stability was not established.
results.quote: Recipient cells resulted hyporesponsive to donor and third-party cells, yet retained reactivity to CMV infection.

results.finding: One intestine-containing multivisceral graft recipient retained CMV reactivity at 41 months after transplantation.
results.detail: Patient #1 had stable, rejection-free graft function and antiviral responses, but continued sirolimus. Intestinal biopsies were analyzed for chimerism; the text does not establish the required histological graft assessment.
results.quote: Recipient cells resulted hyporesponsive to donor and third-party cells, yet retained reactivity to CMV infection.

results.finding: Among 29 fully HLA-matched kidney recipients, 24 stopped immunosuppression; median time off drugs was 48 months.
results.detail: Graft function and surveillance biopsies supported tolerance. Four recipients later resumed drugs: three for recurrent kidney disease and one for rejection.
results.quote: Twenty-four of 29 fully HLA-matched recipients were completely withdrawn from IS drugs after mixed chimerism persisted for at least 6 months.

results.finding: Two HLA-haplotype-matched kidney recipients retained third-party T-cell responses of 9–20% while showing donor hyporesponsiveness.
results.detail: These assays were performed during continued immunosuppression, so they do not establish unrelated immunity after complete withdrawal. Drug-free immune responses in fully matched recipients are cited from previous work.
results.quote: Thus, both patients developed specific unresponsiveness to donor cells in association with IS drug–dependent mixed chimerism.

results.finding: Among 29 fully HLA-matched kidney recipients, 24 withdrew immunosuppression, with a median drug-free duration of 48 months.
results.detail: Several recipients remained off drugs for more than two years, but this was a single-arm study, not a randomized trial.
results.quote: Twenty-three of 24 had no evidence of rejection thereafter during an observation period of up to 10 years.

results.finding: Among 22 HLA-haplotype-matched kidney recipients, 10 achieved reduction to tacrolimus monotherapy; sustained complete withdrawal was not achieved.
results.detail: The prospective cohort met the sample-size requirement, but drug tapering caused loss of chimerism and rejection or reinstitution of maintenance therapy. Most recipients were not drug-free without rejection at 24 months.
results.quote: In 10 of 22 HLA haplotype–matched patients with persistent mixed chimerism for at least 12 months, reduction of IS drugs to tacrolimus monotherapy was achieved.

results.finding: In 3 HLA-identical sibling kidney recipients, 2 maintained stable graft function without rejection for at least 1 year off immunosuppression.
results.detail: Patient 1 briefly resumed mycophenolate for glomerulonephritis before subsequent prolonged withdrawal. Patient 2 was drug-free for 19 months. Patient 3 had only 8–10 months off drugs. No severe infectious complications were reported.
results.quote: The 3 patients have been off immunosuppression for 4 years, 19 months and 8 months, respectively. No rejection or graft-versus-host disease occurred.

results.finding: All 3 drug-free HLA-identical sibling kidney recipients with stable graft function developed protective SARS-CoV-2 vaccine antibody responses.
results.detail: Combined kidney and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation preceded withdrawal. Nine graft biopsies showed no rejection. Vaccination occurred off immunosuppression; all recipients also showed CMV-specific cellular immunity.
results.quote: All three patients developed antibody responses with titers considered to be protective.

results.finding: One HLA-haploidentical kidney recipient developed biopsy-proven acute rejection 127 days after complete immunosuppression withdrawal.
results.detail: Combined kidney and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation induced transient mixed chimerism. Graft function was initially stable off drugs, but rejection occurred before 1 year; maintenance immunosuppression resumed.
results.quote: At 127 days after discontinuation of immunosuppressant (356 days after KT), the serum creatinine level increased abruptly from 0.85 to 2.94 mg/dL, and a kidney biopsy showed acute T cell-mediated rejection, type IIA.

results.finding: One documented rhesus kidney recipient accepted donor skin and rejected third-party skin by 40 days without maintenance immunosuppression.
results.detail: The skin-challenged animal retained its renal allograft. No further immunosuppression was administered after postoperative day 13.
results.quote: Forty days after skin transplantation, the third-party skin was completely rejected, although both host and donor skin grafts remained intact, with no signs of rejection.

results.finding: Of 6 treated rhesus kidney recipients, 3 maintained rejection-free graft survival for 410–880 days, with immunosuppression stopped on day 13.
results.detail: This is an animal result. Graft function remained stable in long-surviving recipients, and no infections or malignancies were observed. The stated criterion does not explicitly require human recipients.
results.quote: Rejection-free survival was prolonged in all treated recipients, and 3 of 6 animals survived long term (410–880 days at study’s end).

results.finding: One studied drug-free rhesus kidney recipient retained third-party T-cell responses while showing donor-specific unresponsiveness.
results.detail: This is an animal result. Long-surviving recipients had stable renal function and preserved graft architecture; third-party skin rejection also demonstrated unrelated immunity. The stated criterion does not explicitly require humans.
results.quote:
In contrast, CD4
+
T cell responsiveness against third-party alloantigens was mostly preserved in the monkey studied here.

results.finding: Foxp3-MSC-treated rat liver recipients (n=3 challenged) accepted donor skin for over 100 days while rejecting third-party skin.
results.detail: Skin challenges occurred 100 days after liver transplantation. Third-party skin was rejected within 14 days. Recipients received Foxp3-MSC monotherapy without maintenance immunosuppressive drugs.
results.quote: BN third-party skin grafts were rejected within 14 days, while LEW donor skin grafts were survived over 100 days (data not shown).

results.finding: Among 5 skin-challenged heart/kidney recipients, 1 accepted donor skin indefinitely while retaining its heart graft; third-party skin was rejected.
results.detail: M4311 retained its heart without maintenance immunosuppression after donor kidney removal and accepted donor skin without histological inflammation.
results.quote: One recipient (M4311) accepted the donor skin graft indefinitely despite previous allonephrectomy, with no histological signs of inflammation or leukocyte infiltration

results.finding: Among 5 skin-challenged heart/kidney recipients, 1 accepted donor skin indefinitely, but its kidney graft had already been removed.
results.detail: The sole indefinite donor-skin acceptor cannot demonstrate simultaneous retention of the kidney graft. Other recipients ultimately rejected donor skin.
results.quote: One recipient (M4311) accepted the donor skin graft indefinitely despite previous allonephrectomy, with no histological signs of inflammation or leukocyte infiltration

results.finding: In the 4-recipient delayed-treatment heart/kidney group, one heart graft remained functional without maintenance immunosuppression for more than 5 years.
results.detail: This is an animal result. The report describes sustained contraction and absence of clinically relevant rejection; it also explicitly describes tolerant recipients off immunosuppression for more than a year.
results.quote: We considered at least some heart/kidney recipients to have achieved tolerance because they maintained well-contracting, rejection-free hearts for more than 5 years.

results.finding: Among 4 delayed-treatment heart/kidney recipients, M8314 had a rejection-free kidney explanted 405 days after donor bone marrow transplantation.
results.detail: Kidney histology supports prolonged acceptance, but the supplied text does not establish stable kidney graft function for a full year after complete drug withdrawal. Native kidneys were retained.

results.finding: All 5 skin-challenged, drug-free heart/kidney recipients rejected third-party skin, demonstrating preserved non-donor immunity.
results.detail: Long-term heart acceptance was assessed by contraction and serial histology. M4311 retained its heart and accepted donor skin while rejecting third-party skin. This is an animal result.
results.quote: All third-party skin allografts were rejected within 8 to 21 days

results.finding: All 5 skin-challenged heart/kidney recipients rejected third-party skin; 3 had already undergone donor kidney removal.
results.detail: Non-donor immunity was preserved, but the supplied text does not establish concurrent stable kidney graft function through clinical, laboratory and histological assessment in the challenged recipients.
results.quote: All third-party skin allografts were rejected within 8 to 21 days

results.finding: Among 37 FCR001-treated kidney recipients, 26 remained off immunosuppression without rejection for 36–123 months.
results.detail: Drug-free recipients had preserved kidney function, normal allograft biopsies and no donor-specific antibodies. Vaccination responses supported retained immunocompetence.
results.quote:
Twenty-six patients were successfully 
taken off IS (time   off   IS   36–123 mo) without rejection.

results.finding: Among 4 tolerant kidney recipients assessed for HBV vaccination, all 3 lacking protective antibodies developed seroconversion/protection.
results.detail: Persistently chimeric recipients were off immunosuppression after FCR001 treatment, with preserved kidney function and normal biopsies. HBV vaccination demonstrated responses to a non-donor antigen.
results.quote:
3 of 4 patients studied 
did not have protective antibodies before vaccination, and 
all 3 had seroconversion/protection postvaccination.

results.finding: Among 37 FCR001-treated kidney recipients, 26 remained drug-free without rejection for 36–123 months.
results.detail: Withdrawal exceeded 2 years, but the phase 2 study was single-arm. Standard-of-care comparators were evaluated retrospectively, not randomized.
results.quote:
Twenty-six patients were successfully 
taken off IS (time   off   IS   36–123 mo) without rejection.

results.finding: In the prospective FCR001 kidney cohort, 26 of 37 recipients achieved sustained drug withdrawal without rejection.
results.detail: Withdrawal occurred around 12 months, with 36–123 months off drugs. Outcomes were examined across HLA disparities, but the supplied text does not quantify the HLA-mismatched denominator or its drug-free, rejection-free fraction at 24 months.
results.quote:
Twenty-six patients were successfully 
taken off IS (time   off   IS   36–123 mo) without rejection.

results.finding: One heart recipient maintained normal graft function without immunosuppression for 5 years, without clinical rejection or overt immunodeficiency.
results.detail: Withdrawal was spontaneous: the recipient stopped his remaining cyclosporine in 2018. Cardiac imaging showed preserved function, and no severe infection requiring hospitalization was reported.
results.quote: The patient clinically exhibits operational tolerance of the transplanted heart for 5 years.

results.finding: One heart recipient, drug-free for 5 years with normal graft function, retained peripheral immune responses to unrelated alloantigens.
results.detail: Alloantigen-induced proliferation was comparable to healthy controls. Tolerance arose spontaneously without a tolerance-inducing intervention, and post-withdrawal graft histology was not reported.
results.quote: it is important that the immune tolerance seems to be graft-specific without systemic immune tolerance, as observed by the preserved allospecific peripheral immune response and the clinical absence of relevant infections.

results.finding: One HLA-mismatched lung recipient maintained rejection-free, stable pulmonary function and protective immunity for over 8 years without immunosuppression.
results.detail: The recipient had SCID and received vertebral bone marrow from the same deceased donor, matched at 1 of 8 HLA alleles. Minimal rejection and transient skin GvHD occurred before complete drug withdrawal.
results.quote: Persistent mixed myeloid chimerism, despite only 1 of 8 HLA match at the allele level, paired with 97%–99% T cell chimerism, has enabled rejection-free, stable pulmonary function, protective immunity, and absence of GvHD for over 8 years without IST.

results.finding: One drug-free lung recipient with stable graft function showed vaccine responses by 3 years after bone marrow transplantation.
results.detail: After complete withdrawal, circulating T cells responded vigorously to third-party cells. Spirometry remained stable, subsequent lung biopsies showed no rejection, and vaccine responses included tetanus, pneumococcal serotypes and SARS-CoV-2.
results.quote: By 3 years after BMT, vaccine responses were detected against tetanus and several of the 16 tested pneumococcal serotypes, and in 2022, against SARS-CoV-2 vaccination (data not shown).

results.finding: Among 20 MDR-101-treated HLA-matched kidney recipients, 15 maintained functional tolerance off all immunosuppression for more than 2 years.
results.detail: The source reports functional tolerance with no death, graft loss, DSA or graft versus host disease. Four recipients resumed immunosuppression for recurrent disease, rejection or borderline biopsy changes.
results.quote: Fifteen (75%) reached the primary study endpoint of IS-free for >2 years.

results.finding: In a randomized trial of 20 MDR-101-treated kidney recipients and 10 controls, 15 treated recipients remained off all immunosuppression for more than 2 years.
results.detail: Recipients received kidneys from two-haplotype HLA-matched living siblings. Withdrawal around 1 year required donor mixed chimerism ≥5%; four recipients subsequently resumed immunosuppression.
results.quote: Fifteen (75%) reached the primary study endpoint of IS-free for >2 years.

results.finding: In A-WISH, 10 of 77 liver recipients remained off all immunosuppression for at least 1 year without clinical rejection.
results.detail: Tolerance was assessed clinically; incomplete biopsies prevent exclusion of subclinical rejection. One recipient required retransplantation for recurrent hepatitis C after 14 months off drugs.
results.quote: Ten subjects (13.0%) remained off all immunosuppression for at least one year with no clinical evidence of rejection and were termed operationally tolerant

results.finding: In randomized A-WISH, 7 of 77 withdrawal-arm liver recipients had documented drug-free follow-up exceeding 2 years.
results.detail: Table 3 records 735–790 days from completion of withdrawal to last laboratory assessment for seven tolerant recipients. The trial randomized 77 recipients to withdrawal and 18 to maintenance.

results.finding: Among 15 ddDCreg-treated liver recipients, 13 were analyzed and 3 maintained stable graft function off all immunosuppression for 3.0 ± 0.17 years.
results.detail: Withdrawal required a permissive biopsy. Three recipients achieved one year off drugs without clinical dysfunction or overt T-cell mediated rejection and remained clinically stable through follow-up.
results.quote:
They also remained
clinically stable, off all IS drugs for 3.0 ± 0.17 years (EOS).

results.finding: Among 11 liver recipients tested at 54 months, donor-reactive T-cell responses were lower than third-party responses; 3 recipients in the clinical cohort were drug-free.
results.detail: The study reports third-party reactivity at the cohort level, combining recipients on and off immunosuppression. The supplied text does not explicitly establish preserved third-party responses in the drug-free recipients individually.
results.quote:
Here, in follow-up, we demonstrate signi ﬁcantly weaker
donor-speciﬁc versus third-party alloimmune responses at 12-months
and at EOS in ddDCreg-infused patients, with reduced pro-
inﬂammatory plasma mediators, such as GM-CSF and IL-12 as com-
pared to the cohorts’ pre-transplant, pre-infusion values.

results.finding: Of 15 treated liver recipients, 13 were analyzed and 3 remained off all immunosuppressive drugs for 3.0 ± 0.17 years.
results.detail: The duration exceeds two years, but this was a single-center, uncontrolled, non-randomized trial.
results.quote:
They also remained
clinically stable, off all IS drugs for 3.0 ± 0.17 years (EOS).

results.finding: In the prospective liver trial, 2 of 12 HLA-mismatched recipients in the analyzed cohort achieved sustained operational tolerance.
results.detail: Table 1 and the reported tolerant patient IDs identify two mismatched successes; the third tolerant recipient had no HLA mismatches. This is below a majority. The exact drug-free, rejection-free outcome at 24 months for all treated mismatched recipients is not reported.

results.finding: Among 8 rat intestinal recipients challenged with skin grafts, 4 accepted donor skin permanently while rejecting third-party skin without maintenance immunosuppression.
results.detail: All 4 ACI recipients met the donor-specific skin challenge criterion with functioning intestinal grafts. Immunosuppression stopped on postoperative day 14; skin challenge occurred after 150 days. The 4 PVG recipients eventually rejected donor skin.
results.quote: Skin grafts from third party donors were rejected promptly. Skin grafts from the original intestinal donor strain had more than doubling of survival (10.5 to 23.5 days) in the 4 PVG recipients, and survived permanently in the 4 ACI recipients

results.finding: Of 10 HLA-mismatched kidney recipients, 4 remained off all immunosuppression for 9–16 years with normal kidney function.
results.detail: Conference abstract published in a journal supplement; the supplied text does not establish peer review of a full paper.
results.quote: Seven of ten subjects were successfully tapered off of all immunosuppression (IS) for >5 years with four of them still IS-free for 9-16 years with normal kidney function.

results.finding: Of 10 HLA-mismatched kidney recipients enrolled in tolerance-induction studies, 7 stopped all immunosuppression for more than 5 years.
results.detail: The abstract does not specify withdrawal timing or freedom from biopsy-proven acute rejection at 24 months after transplantation. Three recipients later restarted immunosuppression for recurrent disease or chronic rejection.
results.quote: Seven of ten subjects were successfully tapered off of all immunosuppression (IS) for >5 years with four of them still IS-free for 9-16 years with normal kidney function.

results.finding: One intestinal transplant recipient maintained stable graft function without rejection or overt immunodeficiency for 5 years off all immunosuppression.
results.detail: Withdrawal was spontaneous against medical advice, approximately 4 years after transplantation. Endoscopy and histology confirmed graft health at follow-up.
results.quote: In contrast, our case demonstrated evidence of clinical organ acceptance (no rejection), immunocompetence to third party antigen, and donor-specific hyporesponsiveness even five years after stopping all immunosuppression.

results.finding: One drug-free intestinal transplant recipient showed normal antiviral T-cell responses and donor-specific hyporesponsiveness with stable graft function.
results.detail: Normal responses to CMV and EBV and reactivity to third-party alloantigens supported immunocompetence. However, tolerance followed spontaneous drug cessation, not a tolerance-inducing intervention.
results.quote: Functional T cell assays revealed that he was otherwise immunocompetent with normal anti-viral CD3+ T cell reactivity against CMV antigen pp65 and Epstein-Barr-Virus (EBV) lysate

results.finding: Among 20 MDR-101-treated kidney recipients, 15 maintained functional immune tolerance without immunosuppression for more than 2 years.
results.detail: Recipients had two-haplotype HLA-matched sibling donors. The report describes no death, graft loss, DSA or graft versus host disease; four recipients resumed immunosuppression.
results.quote: Fifteen (75%) reached the primary study endpoint of IS-free for >2 years.

results.finding: In a randomized trial with 20 treated kidney recipients and 10 controls, 15 treated recipients remained off all immunosuppression for more than 2 years.
results.detail: Withdrawal was conditional on donor mixed chimerism ≥5%. Nineteen stopped all drugs around 1 year after transplantation; four restarted. Recipients were HLA-matched, and unrelated immunity was not tested in the supplied text.
results.quote: Fifteen (75%) reached the primary study endpoint of IS-free for >2 years.

results.finding: Among 36 FCR001-treated HLA-mismatched kidney recipients, 26 (72%) achieved durable immunosuppression withdrawal without biopsy-proven acute rejection.
results.detail: Retrospective follow-up of a prospective phase 2 trial cohort. Immunosuppression was withdrawn by 12 months; withdrawal was durable, and no BPAR occurred in those weaned off through 5 years, encompassing the 24-month threshold.
results.quote:
Among the FCR001
recipients, 26 (72%) developed persistent chimerism allowing durable elimination of
all immunosuppression.

title = "Reliable donor-specific transplantation tolerance". Reason: Rewritten by Claude Fable 5.2 at the owner's request, 15 November 2026. Restores "reliable", the qualifier of the record's title that the page had lost.

definition = "A finite treatment makes most organ recipients who receive it, including those mismatched with their donor for human leukocyte antigens (HLA, the proteins used in tissue matching), accept the graft without maintenance immunosuppression while keeping immune responses to other antigens. Reliability is shown by a multicentre randomized trial, not by selected patients.". Reason: Rewritten by Claude Fable 5.2 at the owner's request, 15 November 2026. The definition described one recipient; the breakthrough is a treatment that works in most recipients, including HLA-mismatched ones.

edit completion: title = "A multicentre randomized trial shows drug-free graft acceptance in most HLA-mismatched recipients."; criterion = "A randomized, controlled, multicentre trial of a tolerance-induction treatment in HLA-mismatched organ recipients meets a prespecified primary endpoint of freedom from all immunosuppression without biopsy-proven acute rejection at least 24 months after transplantation and at least 12 months after complete drug withdrawal. At least 50 recipients are treated and at least half of all those treated reach the endpoint. Drug-free recipients show immune responses to non-donor antigens, for example to vaccination. The result is reported in a peer-reviewed paper or a regulator's review."; set_by = "Technology Atlas. The endpoint is the primary outcome of the FREEDOM-1 phase 3 protocol (NCT03995901), the 12 drug-free months the operational-tolerance convention, and immunocompetence the Immune Tolerance Network objective; the HLA-mismatched scope, 50 treated and one half are the Atlas's."; set_by_kind = "atlas"; threshold_quote = "Proportion of FCR001 recipients who are free from immunosuppression (IS), without biopsy proven acute rejection (BPAR) at 24 months post-transplant"; threshold_ref = 28; basis = "No regulator, society or programme document located states a trial size or success fraction for tolerance induction. The Atlas sets them: half of those treated is the least that \"most recipients\" can mean, and with 50 treated the 95% confidence interval on a proportion near one half is about 14 percentage points either side. HLA-mismatched recipients are required because results in HLA-matched siblings do not carry over to most transplants. Marketing authorization is a separate, later event."; refs = [4, 11, 15, 28]. Reason: Rewritten by Claude Fable 5.2 at the owner's request, 15 November 2026. The test had no scale, so one drug-free patient met it.
